overview: This Senate resolution honors five people who died fighting wildfires in the western United States during the summer of 2026: helicopter crew members Emily Barker, Sydney Watson, Nicholas Hutcherson and Nathan Matthews, who died after responding to fires along the Utah-Colorado border, and firefighting pilot Nicholas Dale of British Columbia, Canada, who died supporting efforts on a Colorado fire. It offers sympathy to their families and colleagues and recognizes firefighters who were injured. More broadly, it thanks wildland firefighters, aviation crews, dispatchers and other support staff, and states that protecting communities from catastrophic fire requires both responsible care of forests and public lands and continued support for firefighters. It does not change any law or spending. The Senate approved it on August 7, 2026.
for: Supporters say the resolution gives deserved national recognition to firefighters who gave their lives protecting others and to the crews who keep facing those dangers each season.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic and doesn't change any law or spending, and that firefighters would be better served by concrete action on pay, staffing and safety.
